newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shr funds see rising inflows so far in July.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shr funds see rising inflows so far in July.

text.p: The flow of money into domestic equity funds is swelling again this month as investors gradually return to Brazilian stocks after the recent strong volatility on local bolsas, asset managers said.

The funds have seen net inflows of 884.91 million reais so far in July, recovering from large withdrawals by retail investors two weeks ago that prompted asset managers to sell heavily in the Sao Paulo bolsa, banking sector data showed.
"We are returning to reasonable levels," said Alfredo Setubal, capital markets vice-president at Banco Itau and director of the National Association of Investment Bankers.

The bleeding of local funds this month hit bottom on July 15 when outflows reached 500 million reais for the day in a week that saw the bolsa reel from a frenetic wave of profit- taking triggered by fears of a devaluation.
Setubal believes the money now flowing into the funds belongs to more experienced investors, who have already recovered from the bolsa's rollercoaster ride.
"The money coming in now is of better quality, from investors who already saw the market's strong price fluctuation and are now taking a long-term perspective," he said.

Despite their positive performance so far in July, equity funds will see lower inflows in the coming months than during the first half of 1997 when massive cash flows helped boost share prices and market turnover, asset managers said.
"Money will keep pouring in, but moderately," said a local asset manager who asked not to be named. "The fund growth in the first half was unexpected."
Domestic equity funds saw accumulated net inflows of 9.1 billion reais in the first half of 1997, against 540 million reais in the same period of last year, according to ANBID's data.
Combined domestic stock fund assets are now estimated at 18.4 billion reais, accounting for about 13 percent of the total industry.
